fields.claim_quote: Therefore $G$ has another subgroup of order $p$, say $H$. Now $H \cap N =1$ and by induction hypotheses  ${\rm dl}(G) \leq {\rm max}\{{\rm dl}(G/N), {\rm dl}(G/H)\} \leq {\rm max}\{|{\rm cod}(G/N)|, |{\rm cod}(G/H)|\} \leq |{\rm cod}(G)|$.
fields.explanation: The original D8, central N={1,r²}, and reflection H={1,s} are preserved as Mathlib DihedralGroup4 and actual Subgroup objects. The theorem proves the group is a noncyclic 2-group of order8, N is central and normal of order2, every nontrivial normal subgroup contains N, and consequently N is the unique minimal normal subgroup. Two distinct involutions and H of order2 satisfy the source noncyclic/extra-subgroup branch. H intersects N trivially but is not normal. Mathlib normality of every homomorphism kernel proves no group homomorphism can have kernel H; hence the printed quotient-group step lacks a necessary hypothesis. The counterexample concerns this local inference, not the main codegree bound.
fields.flaw: After choosing merely another subgroup H of order p, the proof may treat G/H as a quotient group and apply the induction hypothesis to it.
fields.problem: Title: A note on codegrees and Taketa's inequality
fields.witness: Let G=D₈=⟨r,s | r⁴=s²=1, srs=r⁻¹⟩ and p=2. Take N=⟨r²⟩={1,r²}, which is normal, and another order-2 subgroup H=⟨s⟩={1,s}. Then H∩N={1}, but H is not normal: rHr⁻¹=⟨r²s⟩≠H. Moreover, G is a noncyclic 2-group of order 8, and N is its unique minimal nontrivial normal subgroup: every nontrivial normal subgroup contains r^2. These are the source branch hypotheses verified by the selected certificate.

scope_metadata.target_scope: Treating G/H as a quotient group without H normal in the specified p-group branch; not the codegree bound.
